title: Simple Tarka Dal
description: Roughly chopped veg and whichever lentils we have, cooked until soft and mushy. Four portions, with optional coconut milk, spinach, eggs and a Shapla-style tarka if we fancy them.
portionNote: The full batch uses 200 g dry lentils and makes 4 portions. Serve with rice or bread and poppadoms.
imageAlt: Golden tarka dal with softened onion, tomato, mustard seeds, cumin and curry leaves.
personalNote: Ask bubu about the sambar powder and asafoetida if you’re making this alone. We can add coconut milk for a Sri Lankan-style version, or finish with the optional tarka — that’s the bit that adds that Shapla flavour!
equipment: Smallest saucepan for the optional tarka
advancePrep: Wash and soak the dal for at least 15 minutes; longer is fine. Get the spice bowl and roughly chopped veg ready while it soaks. The onions, garlic and tomatoes don’t have to be chopped really fine or look uniform. They’ll soften and cook down while the dal bubbles, so don’t spend ages making everything match.
importantNotes: The cumin seeds, turmeric, sambar powder, first measure of asafoetida and curry leaves all go in the same bowl. Add that bowl after the first covered simmer. The optional tarka has its own extra half-teaspoon of asafoetida; it doesn’t replace the teaspoon in the dal. For spinach dal, add spinach with the spices. For egg dal, add 1 teaspoon garam masala to the spice bowl, then scramble 4 eggs into the finished thick dal until cooked through. Allow a little extra cooking time for the eggs.

steps.title: Wash and soak the dal
steps.description: Wash the yellow dal, green moong dal or whichever lentils we have. Cover with cold water and let it soak for at least 15 minutes. Longer is fine. Get the spice bowl and veg ready while it soaks.
steps.tip: Check the packet for the lentils we’re using too. Whole lentils can need longer to soften than split dal.

steps.title: Make one spice bowl
steps.description: Put the cumin seeds, turmeric, sambar powder, the teaspoon of asafoetida and the handful of curry leaves into a small bowl. Ask bubu about the sambar powder and asafoetida if you’re making this alone. If we’re making egg dal, add the extra teaspoon of garam masala to this bowl too.
steps.tip: Keep this bowl aside for now. It goes into the dal after the first covered simmer, not at the beginning.

steps.title: Rough chopping is fine
steps.description: Roughly chop the onions, the whole head of garlic and the tomatoes. Slit the green chilli. Chop the coriander for later and boil 1 litre of water.
steps.tip: The onions, garlic and tomatoes don’t have to be chopped really fine or look uniform. They’ll soften and cook down while the dal bubbles, so don’t spend ages making everything match.

steps.title: Get the dal and veg into the pot
steps.description: Drain the soaked dal. Put it into a pot on medium heat with the onions, garlic, tomatoes, slit green chilli and the litre of boiled water. Add some salt, mix it all around and bring it to a bubble.

steps.title: Cover and cook until mushy
steps.description: Cover and let it bubble gently for 30 minutes, until the dal and veg are soft and mushy. Give it a stir from time to time so the bottom doesn’t catch.
steps.tip: The 30-minute timer is a check, not a promise for every lentil. If they’re still firm, keep cooking until soft before moving on. Whole green moong may take longer. Add a splash of hot water if it’s drying out, and follow the packet as needed.
steps.doneness: Soft, mushy lentils and veg that have cooked down.

steps.title: Now add the spice bowl
steps.description: Tip everything from the spice bowl into the softened dal and mix it through. Add spinach now if we fancy spinach dal. If we want the coconut version, add the can of coconut milk now too. Let it cook for another 20 minutes until thick, stirring so it doesn’t stick.
steps.heat: Gentle bubbles · lid off to thicken
steps.doneness: Thick dal with the spices cooked through.

steps.title: Taste, then coriander and pepper
steps.description: Taste the dal and adjust the salt. Add the chopped coriander and the ground black pepper, mix it through and cook for another 5 minutes.

steps.title: Optional: scramble in the eggs for egg dal
steps.description: If we’re making egg dal, crack the 4 eggs into the finished thick dal. Keep it on medium-low heat and scramble them through with the spoon until the eggs are cooked through. The extra teaspoon of garam masala should already have gone into the spice bowl. Skip this step if we’re not using eggs.
steps.tip: Give the eggs enough time to cook through; they should be set rather than runny.
steps.doneness: Cooked egg scrambled through the thick dal.

steps.title: Optional: make the tarka for that Shapla flavour
steps.description: If we want the tarka, heat the oil or ghee in the smallest saucepan on medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and the extra half-teaspoon of asafoetida. Let the mustard seeds splutter. Skip this and the next step if we’re not making the tarka.
ingredients: Oil or ghee for the tarka
steps.doneness: Mustard seeds spluttering in the hot oil or ghee.

steps.title: Stir the tarka into the finished dal
steps.description: Take the small saucepan off the heat. Carefully pour the hot oil or ghee mixture into the finished dal — it will sizzle — then mix it around. This adds that Shapla flavour!
ingredients: Oil or ghee for the tarka
steps.heat: Small saucepan off the heat · optional

steps.title: Rice or bread, with poppadoms
steps.description: Serve with rice, naan or parathas and some poppadoms. Whichever combination we fancy.

substitutions.title: Whichever lentils we have
substitutions.text: Use 200 g yellow dal, green moong dal or other lentils. The texture and cooking time will vary, so follow the packet and cook until soft rather than stopping just because the timer is done.

substitutions.title: Coconut milk for a Sri Lankan-style version
substitutions.text: Add 1 can of coconut milk with the spice bowl, then let it cook with the dal during the 20-minute thickening stage.

substitutions.title: The tarka is optional
substitutions.text: Use 2 tablespoons oil or ghee, 1 tablespoon mustard seeds and an extra ½ teaspoon asafoetida. Let it splutter in the smallest saucepan, then carefully stir it into the finished dal. The dal is still ready to eat if we leave this bit out.

substitutions.title: Ask bubu about the two powders
substitutions.text: If you’re making this alone, ask bubu about the sambar powder and asafoetida. The spice bowl uses 2 tablespoons sambar powder and 1 teaspoon asafoetida; the optional tarka uses another ½ teaspoon asafoetida.

substitutions.title: Spinach dal
substitutions.text: Add spinach with the spice bowl and let it cook into the dal during the 20-minute thickening stage.

substitutions.title: Egg dal
substitutions.text: Add 1 teaspoon garam masala to the spice bowl if using eggs. Once the dal is thick and finished with coriander and pepper, crack in 4 eggs and scramble them through on medium-low heat until cooked through.

troubleshooting.title: The lentils are still firm
troubleshooting.text: Keep them gently bubbling until soft and mushy, adding a little hot water if needed. Whole green moong or other whole lentils can take longer than split dal.

troubleshooting.title: Too thick or too thin
troubleshooting.text: If it gets too thick before the lentils are soft, add a little hot water. If it needs thickening after the spice bowl goes in, let it bubble with the lid off, stirring so the bottom doesn’t catch.

storage: Cool any leftover dal quickly and refrigerate within 1–2 hours. Use within 2 days. Keep any saved rice separate and use it within 24 hours.
reheating: Reheat the portion we’re eating once until steaming hot throughout. Add a splash of water if it has thickened in the fridge.
foodSafety: Cook the lentils until fully soft, using their packet instructions as a guide. Take the tarka pan off the heat before carefully pouring the hot mixture into the dal.
servingSuggestion: Four portions with rice, naan or parathas and poppadoms. Add spinach with the spices, or make egg dal with 4 eggs and the extra garam masala. Coconut milk and the finishing tarka are optional too. Serve Chicken 65 alongside the dal for a complete meal; the recipe is linked below.
